entities.name: PMID:10732315
observations: Suzuki, Murata, Jiang, and Power; Journal of the Society for Gynecologic Investigation (2000).
Near-term fetal sheep underwent intermittent hypoxemia with and without 1 hour of intrauterine warming.

entities.name: Hyperthermia blocks hypoxia responses
observations: In normothermic fetal sheep, 30 minutes of hypoxia decreased brain temperature relative to body core, consistent with cerebral hypometabolism and increased cerebral blood flow.
After warming, body-core and brain temperatures rose by 0.66 ± 0.06°C and 0.61 ± 0.10°C; subsequent hypoxia no longer reduced brain temperature relative to body core.
The authors concluded that elevated fetal temperature prevents these compensatory metabolic and cerebral-flow responses and leaves the brain less protected against hypoxic injury.
